title: 🏗️ Monolith vs Microservices — What's the Difference?
excerpt: Should we build everything as one application or split it into smaller services? 🤔
body:
ㅤ
📘 Engineering Notes | From Concepts to Code — Post 10
ㅤ
When building an application, choosing the right architecture is important.

Should we build everything as one application or split it into smaller services? 🤔

Let's explore both using an e-commerce example! 👇
ㅤ
1️⃣ 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 🏢

A monolith combines different features into one deployable application.

For example:

📦 Product Management
🛒 Order Management
👤 User Management
💳 Payment Management

All features run within a single application.

✅ Simple to develop initially
✅ Easier deployment
✅ Straightforward testing

⚠️ As the system grows, maintenance and deployments may become more complex.
ㅤ
2️⃣ 𝗠𝗶𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝗔𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 🌐

Microservices split an application into smaller, independently deployable services.

For example:

📦 Product Service
🛒 Order Service
👤 User Service
💳 Payment Service

Each service handles a specific business capability and communicates through APIs or messages.

✅ Independent deployments
✅ Scale services separately
✅ Clear service ownership

⚠️ More complex communication, monitoring, and infrastructure.
ㅤ
3️⃣ 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹-𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱 𝗘𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲 🛍️

Imagine an e-commerce application receiving heavy order traffic during a sale.

Monolith → We may scale the entire application.

Microservices → We can scale the Order Service independently.

However, microservices introduce distributed system challenges.
ㅤ
4️⃣ 𝗤𝘂𝗶𝗰𝗸 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗻 ⚖️

🔹 Deployment
Monolith → One application
Microservices → Independent services

🔹 Scaling
Monolith → Scale application instances
Microservices → Scale individual services

🔹 Communication
Monolith → Internal method calls
Microservices → APIs or messaging

🔹 Complexity
Monolith → Simpler to start
Microservices → More operational complexity
ㅤ
5️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗵 𝗢𝗻𝗲 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗪𝗲 𝗖𝗵𝗼𝗼𝘀𝗲? 🎯

It depends on project needs, team size, and complexity.

A well-structured monolith is often a good starting point.

Microservices are useful when independent scaling and deployments become important.
ㅤ
💡 𝗠𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

Microservices aren't automatically better than monoliths.

Good architecture means choosing the right solution for the problem.

Sometimes, simplicity is the best engineering decision.
ㅤ
